instruction: assets.id UUID is the true identity; asset_tag is display/source data and must not be assumed unique.
Each asset should have a stable generated QR token independent from the asset tag.
Do not add hundreds of technical columns to assets. Use asset types, attribute definitions, and attribute values.
Support multiple design/performance profiles for one physical asset, such as cooling and heating performance.
Support parent/child and equipment-to-equipment relationships such as contains, component_of, serves, fed_by, related, backup_of.
Support Shop Drawing, Floorplan, Specification, O&M Manual, Commissioning and Other documents.
Import real equipment records even when asset_tag is blank; generate UUID identity and QR token.
Do not merge records just because asset_tag matches. Use section, location, description, and source row.
When the same HC-CC-* designation occurs in both changeover cooling-performance and heating-performance sections, create one asset with two design profiles.
The spreadsheet STATUS field is engineering/source information and must not automatically overwrite app workflow status.
Only create relationship links automatically when the referenced equipment can be identified confidently; otherwise keep the source value and flag for review.
QR labels should resolve through /q/:token to the correct asset, including switching current project if the user has access.
If a logged-out user opens a QR deep link, login must return to the original QR URL.
Remove manual QR Code ID input from normal asset creation.
Asset detail should include Overview, Technical/Design, Service, Electrical & Controls, Documents, and Activity.
Technical/Service/Electrical fields must render dynamically from attribute definitions based on asset type.
Keep forms and asset detail mobile-friendly because QR scanning will commonly happen from phones.
Preserve existing projects, assets, locations, systems, statuses, issues, timeline/events, photos, notes, tags, users, QR scanning and CSV importing.
